mainTopic: Can a יורש do ביטול רשות in a courtyard on שבת when he inherits on שבת itself?
overview: רבא asks רב נחמן whether an heir who inherits a share in a courtyard on שבת may do ביטול רשות. Maybe he cannot, because he could not have made an עירוב before שבת. Or maybe he can, because a יורש stands in his father's place. רב נחמן says the heir can renounce, though the school of שמואל taught that he cannot. רבא challenges him with a ברייתא: whatever was permitted or forbidden at the start of שבת stays that way all שבת, except for one who renounces his rights. The גמרא explains the ברייתא's examples and then draws the inference that only the owner himself is excepted, not an heir. רב נחמן answers that the exception covers the whole category of renouncing, which includes heirs. A second ברייתא says an heir 'forbids' carrying, and רב נחמן explains this means he forbids only until he renounces. The amud ends as the גמרא begins a new challenge about a Jew and a גר who shared one residence, and it continues on the next amud.

steps.title: First side: maybe the heir cannot renounce
steps.stepSummary: Maybe ביטול רשות is only allowed for someone who could have made an עירוב before שבת. The heir was not a resident then, so maybe he cannot renounce now.
steps.simpleTranslation: A person who could have made an עירוב yesterday (before שבת) can also renounce his rights today. But this heir could not have made an עירוב yesterday, so he cannot renounce today either.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains one possible reason why an heir would NOT be allowed to do ביטול רשות. This is the first half of a two-sided question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The logic links ביטול רשות to עירוב. Renouncing on שבת works as a backup for someone who could have made an עירוב before שבת but did not. The heir only became a resident on שבת, so before שבת he had no power to make an עירוב, and maybe he has no power to renounce either.

keyTerms.meaning: to make an עירוב (joining the courtyard residents so they may carry)
from yesterday, meaning before שבת began
to renounce one's rights in the courtyard (ביטול רשות)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the גמרא's conclusion. It is only one side of רבא's question, and the other side comes next.

phrases.english: Where, if he wanted to make an eiruv yesterday,
he could have made an eiruv,
he can also renounce;
but this one (the heir), since
if he had wanted to make an eiruv yesterday
he could not have made an eiruv,
he cannot renounce.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכָא דְּאִי בָּעֵי לְעָרוֹבֵי מֵאֶתְמוֹל מָצֵי מְעָרֵב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Lays out the first side of רבא's question (יורש מהו שיבטל רשות), which began on the previous amud.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does ביטול רשות depend on having been able to make an עירוב before שבת?

steps.title: Second side: maybe the heir is like his father
steps.stepSummary: Or maybe a יורש is an extension of his father. Since the father could have renounced, so can the heir.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or perhaps an heir is like his father's foot, a continuation of him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the opposite side of the question: maybe the heir simply takes his father's place. This finishes the two-sided question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the יורש counts as a continuation of the father, then what matters is the father's status. The father was a resident before שבת and could have made an עירוב or renounced, so the heir inherits that ability.

keyTerms.meaning: or perhaps (introduces the other side of a question)
his father's foot, meaning a direct extension of the father

steps.whyThisMatters: The idea יורש כרעיה דאבוה הוא is a general principle that shows up in other places in ש״ס.

phrases.english: Or perhaps:
an heir is his father's foot (an extension of him)?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers the opposite side to Step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the heir judged by his father's pre-שבת status?

steps.title: רב נחמן: I say he can renounce, but the school of שמואל says he cannot
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that in his own view the heir can renounce. The school of שמואל, however, taught that he cannot.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said to him: I say he can renounce. But those of the school of שמואל taught that he cannot renounce.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers רבא's question by giving his own opinion that the heir can renounce. He also reports that the school of שמואל disagrees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן sides with the 'heir is like his father' approach. The school of שמואל follows the first approach, that one who could not make an עירוב before שבת cannot renounce.

phrases.english: He said to him: I say he can renounce,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָנֵי דְּבֵי שְׁמוּאֵל תָּנוּ אֵין מְבַטֵּל.
phrases.english: while those of the school of Shmuel taught: he cannot renounce.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the two-sided question of Steps 1–2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב נחמן: the heir can renounce. The school of שמואל: he cannot.

steps.title: רבא objects from a general rule about part of שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבא cites a ברייתא: whatever is permitted or forbidden at part of שבת stays that way all of שבת, except for one who does ביטול רשות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא challenged him from a ברייתא: This is the rule. Anything permitted for part of שבת is permitted for all of שבת. Anything forbidden for part of שבת is forbidden for all of שבת. The exception is one who renounces his rights.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא raises an objection to רב נחמן by quoting a ברייתא. The ברייתא gives a general rule with one exception, ביטול רשות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule says the status at the start of שבת locks in for the whole שבת. ביטול רשות is the only stated exception that can change things midway. רבא will use this ברייתא against רב נחמן's view about the heir, and the exact point of attack unfolds as the גמרא explains each clause.

keyTerms.meaning: he raised an objection to him (from a תנאי source)
one's rights or domain in the courtyard

phrases.english: He raised an objection: This is the principle:
anything that is permitted for part of Shabbat
is permitted for all of Shabbat,
and anything that is prohibited for part of Shabbat
is prohibited for all of Shabbat,
except for one who renounces his rights.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב נחמן's ruling in Step 3 using a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's view that an heir can renounce.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא's framework of status fixed at the start of שבת, with ביטול רשות as the only exception, will be shown to conflict with רב נחמן's view once its clauses are explained.

steps.title: Explaining the first clause: an עירוב stays valid even if the opening is closed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins explaining the ברייתא. If an עירוב was made through a doorway or window that was then blocked on שבת, carrying stays permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Anything permitted for part of שבת is permitted for all of שבת.' For example, an עירוב was made through a doorway, and the doorway was closed up. Or an עירוב was made through a window, and the window was closed up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts going through the ברייתא clause by clause, beginning with the 'permitted' clause. This is setup for the next clauses, where רבא's challenge will come into focus.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two courtyards joined by an עירוב through a doorway or window were allowed to carry when שבת began. Even though the connection was blocked during שבת, the permission that existed at the start continues all שבת.

phrases.english: Anything that was permitted for part of Shabbat
is permitted for all of Shabbat:
for example, he made an eiruv via the doorway,
and the doorway was closed up;
he made an eiruv via a window,
and the window was closed up.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל שֶׁהוּתַּר לְמִקְּצָת שַׁבָּת, מוּתָּר לְכׇל הַשַּׁבָּת — כְּגוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first clause of the ברייתא quoted in Step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Once carrying was permitted at the start of שבת through an עירוב, closing the opening during שבת does not cancel it.

steps.title: Adding an alleyway that lost its beam or post
steps.stepSummary: The words זה הכלל in the ברייתא come to include a מבוי whose קורה or לחי was removed on שבת. Carrying there stays permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'This is the rule' comes to include an alleyway whose beams or side posts were taken away.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps explaining the first half of the ברייתא ('permitted for part of שבת, permitted all שבת'). It says the extra words זה הכלל add one more case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מבוי needs a קורה or a לחי to be allowed for carrying. If it had one when שבת began and it was removed on שבת, the alley stays permitted. Like the blocked window in step 5, a change on שבת does not cancel a status that was set at the start.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This is the rule', a phrase that adds more cases
to include, to add another case
an alleyway that courtyards open into
a crossbeam over the alley entrance
a side post at the alley entrance

phrases.english: 'This is the rule'
comes to include an alleyway
whose beams or side posts were removed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues explaining the permissive half of the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מבוי that lost its קורה or לחי on שבת stays permitted for carrying for the rest of שבת.

steps.title: The forbidden half: two houses walled in on שבת
steps.stepSummary: Whatever was forbidden at part of שבת stays forbidden. The example is two houses across a רשות הרבים that גוים walled in on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Anything forbidden for part of שבת is forbidden for all of שבת. For example, two houses on two sides of a public area, and non-Jews built a wall around them on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now explains the second half of the ברייתא, the forbidden side, and gives an example.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before שבת the two houses were separated by a רשות הרבים, so they could not make an עירוב together. Once the wall goes up on שבת, the enclosed area becomes a proper private area. It still stays forbidden, because carrying there was forbidden when שבת began.

phrases.english: Anything forbidden for part of Shabbat
is forbidden for the whole of Shabbat
for example, two houses
on two sides of a public domain
and non-Jews surrounded them with a wall on Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the permissive half of the ברייתא to the forbidden half.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An area that could not have an עירוב when שבת began stays forbidden, even if a proper wall is built on שבת.

steps.title: What does the second 'this is the rule' add?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what extra case the second זה הכלל comes to include.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'This is the rule' comes to include what?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question about the wording. It is setting up the next step, which gives the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase זה הכלל appears again, in the forbidden half of the ברייתא. Since every phrase should teach something, the גמרא looks for the new case it adds.

phrases.english: 'This is the rule', to include what?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the extra wording in the forbidden half.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which case is added by the second זה הכלל.

steps.title: A non-Jew who died on שבת
steps.stepSummary: It adds a גוי living in the חצר who died on שבת without renting out his share. The חצר stays forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to include a non-Jew who died on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the extra phrase adds the case of a גוי neighbor who died on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While the גוי was alive, his presence blocked an עירוב, so carrying was forbidden when שבת began. His death on שבת removes the problem, but the חצר still stays forbidden for the rest of שבת.

phrases.english: To include a non-Jew who died on Shabbat.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The second זה הכלל includes a גוי resident who died on שבת. The חצר stays forbidden.

steps.title: Only the owner himself, not the heir
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא makes an exception only for the one who does ביטול רשות. That suggests the owner himself may renounce on שבת, but a יורש may not. This goes against רב נחמן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it teaches: 'except for one who renounces his rights.' He himself, yes. An heir, no.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא now reaches the real point of quoting the ברייתא. He uses its exception clause to challenge רב נחמן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everything forbidden at the start of שבת stays forbidden, with one exception: ביטול רשות. The exception speaks of the owner who renounces. רבא reads this to mean that only the original resident can renounce on שבת. A יורש, who was not a resident when שבת began, falls back under the main rule and cannot. That directly contradicts רב נחמן's answer in step 3.
steps.whatToRemember: רבא's ברייתא says a status set at the start of שבת stays all שבת. Only the person who himself does ביטול רשות is an exception, which implies a יורש is not. This challenges רב נחמן.
steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא never says 'an heir cannot.' רבא is drawing an inference from what it leaves out: it mentions only the owner who renounces.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the core of the challenge to רב נחמן, and it supports the view of the school of שמואל from step 3.

phrases.english: And it teaches: except for one who renounces his rights.
He himself, yes
an heir, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining the ברייתא in steps 5 to 9, returns to רבא's challenge against רב נחמן.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's ruling that a יורש can do ביטול רשות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא's exception speaks only of the original owner who renounces. So a יורש, who was not a resident at the start of שבת, stays under the rule that what was forbidden stays forbidden.

steps.title: Read the exception as a whole category of renouncing
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן rereads the ברייתא: the exception covers the whole category of ביטול רשות, not only the original owner.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say it like this: 'except for anything that falls under the category of ביטול רשות.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers the challenge from Step 10 by changing how we read the ברייתא's exception.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed that 'except for the one who renounces' meant only the owner himself. רב נחמן says to read it as 'except for the category of renouncing.' That category also includes a יורש, so his ruling stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Say / read it this way (introduces a new reading of a text)
The category or legal framework of
Renouncing one's rights in a shared courtyard so the others may carry

phrases.english: Say [it this way]:
phrases.notes: רב נחמן is the speaker, answering the challenge from Step 10.

phrases.english: except for the category of renouncing rights.
phrases.notes: A category, not one particular person, so an heir is included.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The exception covered only the person who personally owned the share at the start of שבת.
steps.terutzMaskana: The exception covers anyone in the category of renouncing, including a יורש.

steps.title: A new source: a resident dies and leaves his share to an outsider
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא is brought against רב נחמן. Its first case: a resident of the courtyard dies and leaves his share to an outsider.
steps.simpleTranslation: He challenged him: If one of the courtyard's residents died and left his share to someone from the marketplace, then if he died while it was still day, the heir forbids carrying. If he died after dark, the heir does not forbid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new challenge by quoting a ברייתא. This step is setup; the actual question comes in Step 14.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the resident died before שבת, the outsider owned the share when שבת began. He made no עירוב, so he forbids carrying. If the resident died after dark, the courtyard was permitted when שבת began, and it stays permitted. This is the rule from the ברייתא in Steps 4–5: whatever is permitted for part of שבת stays permitted for all of שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: He challenged him from a תנאי source
From the marketplace, meaning an outsider who does not live in the courtyard
While it is still day, before שבת begins
After dark, once שבת has begun

steps.confusionAlert: 'Forbids' and 'does not forbid' describe the heir's effect on the whole courtyard. They do not describe whether the heir himself may carry.

phrases.english: He challenged him:
phrases.notes: According to the reference translation, רבא challenges רב נחמן.

phrases.english: one of the courtyard residents who died,
and left his share to someone from the marketplace,
[if he died] while still day, [the heir] forbids,
phrases.notes: The heir owned the share when שבת began and made no עירוב.

phrases.english: after dark, he does not forbid.
phrases.notes: It was permitted at the start of שבת, so it stays permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new challenge after Step 11's answer
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's ruling that a יורש may do ביטול רשות on שבת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup only. The ברייתא's ruling that the heir 'forbids' will be used against רב נחמן in Step 14.

steps.title: The reverse case: an outsider dies and leaves his share to a resident
steps.stepSummary: The second case of the ברייתא: an outsider who owned a share in the courtyard dies and leaves it to a resident.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if someone from the marketplace died and left his share to one of the courtyard's residents, then if he died while still day, it does not forbid. If he died after dark, it forbids.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with the reverse case. This is still setup for the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the outsider died before שבת, the resident inherits in time, and his own עירוב covers the new share. If the outsider died after dark, the share was forbidden when שבת began, so it stays forbidden. Here the heir received his share on שבת itself, which is exactly the case רב נחמן ruled on.

phrases.english: And someone from the marketplace who died
and left his share to one of the courtyard residents,
[if he died] while still day, it does not forbid,
phrases.notes: The resident's עירוב covers his new share.

phrases.english: after dark, it forbids.
phrases.notes: Forbidden at the start of שבת, so it stays forbidden. Compare Step 7.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֶחָד מִן הַשּׁוּק שֶׁמֵּת וְהִנִּיחַ רְשׁוּתוֹ לְאֶחָד מִבְּנֵי חָצֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues quoting the ברייתא begun in Step 12
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An outsider's share inherited by a resident after dark forbids carrying for the rest of that שבת.

steps.title: Why forbid? Let the heir renounce
steps.stepSummary: The challenge: if an heir may renounce on שבת, why does the ברייתא simply say he 'forbids'?
steps.simpleTranslation: Why does it forbid? Let him renounce!
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא makes its actual attack. If רב נחמן is right, the heir could just renounce his share, so the ברייתא should not say flatly that he forbids.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says 'forbids' as if nothing can fix the problem. The question is aimed at the first case, where the outsider who inherited the share forbids carrying. According to רב נחמן, an heir may renounce, so the heir could easily solve it with ביטול רשות.

phrases.english: Why does he forbid?
Let him renounce!
phrases.notes: According to רב נחמן, an heir may renounce on שבת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the ברייתא of Steps 12–13 into a challenge
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's ruling that a יורש may do ביטול רשות on שבת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא rules flatly that the heir forbids carrying. That suggests renouncing is not an option for him, which contradicts רב נחמן.

steps.title: 'Forbids' means 'forbids until he renounces'
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that 'forbids' means the heir forbids carrying only until he renounces his share.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does the 'forbids' that it teaches mean? It forbids until he renounces.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן defends his view by explaining what the word 'forbids' in the ברייתא really means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא only means that an עירוב can no longer fix the problem on שבת. It does not rule out ביטול רשות. So the heir forbids carrying only until he renounces, and רב נחמן's ruling stands.
steps.whatToRemember: רב נחמן holds that a יורש may renounce on שבת. He survives both challenges by rereading the sources: 'renouncing' is a category that includes heirs, and 'forbids' means 'forbids until he renounces.'

phrases.english: What is the 'forbids' that it teaches?
[It forbids] until he renounces.
phrases.notes: An עירוב cannot fix it, but ביטול רשות can.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי אוֹסֵר נָמֵי דְּקָתָנֵי עַד שֶׁיְּבַטֵּל
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining a word in the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Forbids' meant forbidden for the whole שבת with no possible fix.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Forbids' means only until he renounces, so renouncing remains possible for the heir.

steps.title: A new source: a Jew and a convert sharing one residence
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new challenge to רב נחמן with a ברייתא about a Jew and a גר who live together, where the גר dies before שבת begins.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: a Jew and a convert were living in one residence, and the convert died while it was still day (before שבת).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is starting a new challenge against רב נחמן by quoting the opening case of a ברייתא. This line only sets up the case; the ruling and the challenge come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גר who has no children born after his conversion has no legal heirs. When he dies, his property becomes ownerless, and whoever takes it first acquires it. The גמרא wants to see what the ברייתא says about a Jew who takes over the dead גר's space, and whether that fits רב נחמן's view on renouncing on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: "Come and hear." This introduces a source brought as a proof or a challenge.
A convert. If he dies without children born after his conversion, he has no heirs.
A residence or living space, here shared by two people.
While it is still day, meaning before שבת begins.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume the dead גר's share goes to an heir, as in the previous ברייתא. A גר without children has no heirs at all. His property is ownerless, and the first person to take it acquires it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This case differs from the inheritance cases in steps 12 and 13. Here the Jew gains the share by taking ownerless property, not by inheriting it. That gives the גמרא a fresh angle for testing רב נחמן's rule about ביטול רשות.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
phrases.notes: This introduces a new ברייתא brought against רב נחמן.

phrases.english: a Jew and a convert were living in a single residence,
phrases.notes: The residence has several rooms that share common space.

phrases.english: and the convert died while it was still day,
phrases.notes: He died before שבת and left no heirs, so his property is ownerless.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רב נחמן answered the challenge from the heir ברייתא (step 15), the גמרא opens a fresh challenge from a different ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's position that someone who gains a share in the courtyard on שבת can renounce it (ביטול רשות).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This is only the setup so far. The ruling of the ברייתא about the Jew who takes the גר's property will be checked against רב נחמן's view in the next lines.
